chunks.content: ## Adding Ribbing in CLO: Step-by-Step Tutorial This section details the process of adding ribbing to a garment in CLO 3D software, covering file management, sewing techniques, fold arrangements, fabric application, and simulation adjustments. ### Opening and Preparing Files - Open the **practice files folder** in the library window. - Locate the file named **C.Details.C.EditRibbon**. - Drag this file into either the **2D or 3D window** within the **T-shirt wrap folder**. - In the **3D T-shirt wrap folder**, select the **display arrangement point**. - Place the ribbon onto this arrangement point for further editing. ### Sewing the Ribbon to the Sleeve - In the **purple wrap folder**, accessed via the **attribute editor**, adjust the ribbon’s version location as needed. - Use the **free sewing line tool** to join the ribbon to the sleeve. This step must be repeated to ensure a secure attachment. - After sewing, use the **full ribbon tool** to create fold lines along the sides of the ribbon. ### Creating Fold Arrangements - Select the **fold arrangement tool** from the 3D tool list. - Click on the newly created fold line to activate the **fold arrangement location tool**. - Use the arrow control to half-fold the ribbon, which shapes the ribbing fold realistically. - This procedure creates the fold arrangement necessary for the ribbing effect. ### Sewing and Adjusting Fold Lines - Use the **line sewing tool** to sew the pattern on both the top and bottom sides. - In the **attribute editor**, change the sewing line type to **TEND** to improve simulation results. - After running the simulation, the pattern will appear more even and natural. - Use the **editor tool** to select the newly created inner line of the fold. - Adjust the folding angle to **0 degrees** in the attribute editor to flatten the fold. - Activate simulation again to apply these settings to the 3D clothing. ### Applying Fabric and Pattern Adjustments - Enter the **drawing window** and double-click the **Fabric file**. - Press and hold the **Ripe 2x2** fabric pattern, then drag and release it onto the pattern in either the 2D or 3D window to apply the material. - Activate simulation to visualize the fabric on the garment. - Use the **adjustment panel tool** in the 2D window to select the heavy pattern. - Press and hold the **Ripe 2x2** fabric again, align the pattern, and copy it as needed. - In the 3D window, use the **positioning tool** to move the pattern precisely to the model’s wrist area. ### Final Sewing and Support Adjustments - Use the **line sewing tool** to sew the pattern onto the sleeve and supports. - In the 3D window, use the **measurement tool** to adjust and add the pattern to the supports, ensuring accurate fit and structure. - Activate simulation to finalize the garment’s appearance with the ribbing applied. ### Verification and Execution - Confirm the checkmark on the top of the skirt to ensure correct settings.
